proposal.summary: IOAccelCommandQueue2::processSegmentKernelCommand() performs incorrect size checks that exclude an 8-byte IOAccelKernelCommand header, allowing parsing to read up to 8 bytes out-of-bounds. Command type 2 (kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp) writes timestamp data into this out-of-bounds memory, making the write visible to userspace via shared memory. A PoC triggers the issue on iOS 13 (iPod9,1 17B111).
proposal.affected_product: Apple iOS (iOS 13 on iPod9,1 17B111); macOS possibly affected (report indicates similar code paths)
proposal.cwe_quote: When verifying that the size of the IOAccelKernelCommand has enough data for the specific command type, it appears that the check excludes the size of the 8-byte header, meaning that processSegmentKernelCommand() will parse up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds data.

AV.quote: The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.

PR.quote: The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.

C.quote: command type 2 corresponds to kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp, which actually *writes* into the OOB memory rather than just parsing data from it.

A.quote: This makes it possible to overwrite the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page of memory with timestamp data.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Reproduce locally using the provided PoC on the reported iOS build, confirm exact memory layout and which user-controlled fields allow triggering the write. Patch by including the 8-byte header in bounds checks (or otherwise validating command sizes) and audit other shared-memory parsing for similar double-fetch or non-volatile reads.
